newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks finish higher on bank rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks finish higher on bank rally.

* Toronto stocks ended higher on Thursday, spurred by a rally in bank stocks * Investors await key U.S. jobless data on Friday * 112 million shares traded worth C$1.9 billion
Toronto stocks ended higher on Thursday as bulging bank profits sparked a buying spree in the heavyweight financial services group.

The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 11.61 points to close at 6214.73, extending Wednesday's rally sparked by market-soothing comments from U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan. Trading was brisk with 112.4 million shares changing hands worth C$1.9 billion. Advancing stocks outpaced declines 525 to 432, with 278 issues unchanged.
"The banks are the engine that's fueling our market for the time being," said Montreal-based stock analyst Bill Ram.
The TSE's financial services group added more than 110 points to a 52-week high of 6341.95 as Canada's big six banks wrapped up a record first quarter.
Bank shares rallied after Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce posted a 12 percent increase in first-quarter profit on Thursday and announced plans for a stock split.

Meanwhile, investors will be looking for signs of inflation when key U.S. jobless numbers are released on Friday. "Greenspan has soothed the feathers a bit, so we'd have to come up with pretty negative numbers to see inflationary pressures," Ram said.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* CIBC led the bank rally, up 2 to close at 69.10 on 2.4 million shares after hitting a 52-week high of 69.15.
Royal Bank of Canada added 1.50 to 59.20 on 2.5 million shares, off a 52-week peak of 59.70. Bank of Montreal rose 1.45 to 52.05 on 1.4 million shares after a high of 52.20.
* Oil company Petro-Canada topped the TSE's most-active list, up 0.20 to 19.95 on 5.2 million shares.
* Canadian funeral home operator Loewen Group Inc sank 1.95 to 43.50 after a brokerage downgraded the stock to a buy from a strong buy after fourth-quarter results on Wednesday.
